parsed.explanation: Strong legal infrastructure and broad social acceptance (working courts granting relief, hate-crime enhancement, public LGBTQ visibility, 250k-Pride-scale life) coexist with real traveler-facing exposures. The main airport has no trans-interaction regulations and a documented 2023 case of humiliating screening, with officials demanding surgery for gender recognition — a recurring, universal-exposure point for any trans traveller who is questioned. The default custody practice is isolation/segregation rather than identity-based placement, and no statute covers gender identity in anti-discrimination law, so recourse is thin. 2025 data shows 433 homophobic/transphobic incidents including organised dating-app ambushes, with trans people 'bearing the brunt' — a current, patterned violence signal, though raw counts without denominators and no state targeting keep it below the organised-campaign tier. No facility ban, no criminalisation, courts do grant relief (2019 prison transfer). Net: acceptance plus functioning institutions, but with an unremedied screening exposure and elevated recent violence — reduced-risk with material deductions, 0.60.
